text:
B: Hiya! Oh, it's the Forest lad. I'm Gemma.
A: Liam. Alright? You're the teacher, yeah? Kerry said.
B: Ha, I'm getting a reputation. Yeah, Head of Maths. I'm in Beeston.
A: Ilkeston, me. Proper local. And finally, someone who says cob.
B: Oh, thank God! I've had barm off both the Warrington ones and Kerry looking at me like I'd made it up. It's a cob, isn't it?
A: It's a cob. I told Kerry she was wrong and she would not have it.
B: I heard! Erm, you might want to go a bit easier, duck, she's had a long day. But you're not wrong.
A: She were alright. Blunt, I like that. So you've got Forest in the house, then?
B: My husband Rob and my son Josh have got season tickets. If they lose, the whole house goes mardy for the weekend. I just keep my head down and walk the dog.
A: That's me and my dad. Honestly, that's about all we talk about, Forest and work. He were a fitter, factory's long gone now.
B: Oh, my dad was a fitter as well, in Derby. Same sort of family, by the sound of it.
A: Yeah? There you go. And your fella's a sparky, the other Liam said.
B: Self-employed, yeah. Can I be honest with you? He loves it, but the paperwork nearly killed him the first year. VAT, insurance, all the certificates. I ended up doing his spreadsheets at the kitchen table at midnight, so if you're going on your own, sort that side out first, don't just wing it.
A: Nah, I'll get an accountant, it's fine.
B: That's what Rob said.
A: Ha! Alright, point taken. What's he do, domestic?
B: Mostly, yeah, rewires, bit of solar now. Sorry, I'm going on, you don't want my husband's business plan.
A: Nah, it's useful. What else do you do, then, when you're not marking?
B: Erm, not much, honestly. Parkrun at Colwick if I can drag myself out, walk the dog round Attenborough. Bake Off with my daughter. I'm not very exciting.
A: Attenborough's good for photos, actually. I take pictures of old buildings, murals and that. There's one in Sneinton, massive, all colours, I've been back about five times. Everyone thinks I'm just a gym lad, but I've been to Nottingham Contemporary loads.
B: Oh, I'd never have guessed that. Did you do art at school?
A: Got a B. Only one I got. Left at sixteen, went straight into the apprenticeship.
B: Well, you could still do something with it. We've got adults doing evening courses at the college all the time. You'd be surprised who turns up.
A: Yeah, I've thought about it, sort of. Never got round to it.
B: You should. Honestly, you remind me of the lads I went to school with, and half of them were cleverer than anyone gave them credit for.
A: That's nice of you to say, that. Are your kids into art?
B: Josh is into Xbox and chicken nuggets. Maisie's on her phone all day, which worries me, if I'm honest. You don't know who they're talking to, do you know what I mean?
A: Nah, you don't. I'm glad I didn't have all that at fifteen. I'd have been...
